full_judgment:
7. Mr Khair, the learned Advocate, submits that after expiry of 90 days as per provision of the Limitation Act, in fact, the instant suit has been abated. Without prayer for setting aside the abatement the application for transposition of the name of the defendant No.4 in the category of plaintiff was not maintainable. He submits that the second application for transposition was also not maintainable. He finally submits that if the defendant No.4 is found to be aggrieved by the impugned deed he can file a fresh suit. The learned Trial Court rightly rejected the application for transposition. 

 20. Mr Kbair submits that as per provisions of Article 176 of the Limitation Act the instant suit has been abated after 90 days of the death of the sole plaintiff. While assailing the submissjon of Mr Kbair, Mr Abul Kalam Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that since all the heirs of the deceased plaintiff are already on record and the defendant No.4 petitioner filed application for transposition of his name in the category of the plaintiff, the question of abatement in the instant suit does not arise at all. In support of his submission Mr Chowdhury at first cited the case of People's Republic of Bangladesh vs Abul Kaiser Choudhury, reported in 37 DLR (AD) 85. In the said case it has been observed by their Lordships of the Appellate Division.
